findings.reason: Generated artifacts replace three checked-in JSON files, but no native check re-derives the emitted JSON byte-for-byte against the original source at 7d1d7bec81d96752b5a9a235044d2dfc3ecd259b; the recorded 'configuration_equivalence' is an assertion over parsed JSON, not a native binding, so independent value-level preservation of permissions, QM/B, queue sizes, subscribers and instance specifiers remains unverified.

The integration profile previously emitted a separately packaged mw_com_config.json under tests/utils/environments; the claim 'original_etc_filename_and_JSON_preserved' is a self-reported assertion with no native evidence reference tying the packaged runtime/runfile path to the original installation location, leaving package/output path preservation unmeasured.

Consumer target ilm_control_UT keeps 'src/details/test_lmcontrol_mw_com_config.json' as both an args rootpath and data source that is now the declared output of mw_com_config in the same package; correctness depends on Bazel resolving the generated file ahead of the deleted checked-in path, which is build-order behavior not covered by a distinct native check.

_render injects 'global' keyed by profile while the LM_CONTROL client instance uses asil-level 'B' and strict permission-checks with allowedProvider B:[3020]; equivalence checks cover parsed JSON equality but not semantic admissibility of these safety/QM parameters, which is outside the measured scope.

Profile-name keys in _SERVICE_TYPES/_SERVICE_INSTANCES/_GLOBAL are disclosure metadata, so any future addition of a profile silently emits a new root document; the deduplication consolidates three files into one module but introduces a single-point variance surface without a native regression guard on the emitted document set.
